reason: Narrow, one-system link: the VUV comb mainly serves the 229Th clock itself, not a structural link in both fields. Strength 2.
Quantum multipole selection rules and Weisskopf estimates are a shared mechanism, not a one-to-one identity: quantum transition moments and the classical antenna formula differ in regime.
Same coherence/formation-time physics, generalized to non-Abelian radiation, so a mechanism rather than an analogy.
Detection uses these cross sections, but photoabsorption is not Klein–Nishina scattering and the link is application of known cross sections, not an identity.
Low-energy theorem is shared, but nucleon structure (polarizabilities) and DVCS kinematics differ, so not an identity.
Not an identity: the QCD critical point is conjectured, and the nuclear liquid–gas transition has different microscopic origin. Shared Ising universality makes it an analogy.

fix.summary: Nuclear matter has a liquid–gas first-order line ending in a critical point (T_c≈15–20 MeV near saturation density). A conjectured QCD critical endpoint at high μ_B would share its Ising (Z₂) universality class. Both are analysed with Gibbs coexistence in (T, μ_B).
fix.breaks: The QCD endpoint is conjectured, not observed. Its Z₂ is emergent from chiral/deconfinement dynamics, while the liquid–gas transition comes from nucleon interactions; finite nuclei blur the nuclear one.

reason: Spin glasses are not a clear RMT descendant; keep the well-established mesoscopic and quantum-chaos applications.

fix.summary: Wigner introduced random matrices to model the dense resonances of compound nuclei. Level-spacing repulsion (Wigner surmise) and Porter–Thomas width distributions, after Dyson's classification, became core tools for mesoscopic transport, localization and quantum chaos.

reason: duplicate of C1754
Ideal-gas limit only; real QGP deviates, so not an identity. Map wrongly gives pion-gas ε/T⁴≈3; it is 3π²/30≈1.
Neutron chains are a branching process, but the mean-field DP-class claim needs a saturating nonlinearity that linear reactor physics lacks.

fix.summary: A neutron chain reaction is a Galton–Watson branching process, and k_eff=1 is its critical point, with zero population absorbing. Adding a saturating nonlinearity puts it in the mean-field directed-percolation class. Reactor-noise methods (Feynman-α, Rossi-α) use the diverging fluctuations near k=1 to measure subcriticality.

reason: BK has a nonlocal BFKL kernel and is only in the FKPP universality class after a diffusion expansion; not an identity.

fix.breaks: BK uses the full nonlocal BFKL kernel; it maps onto FKPP only after expanding to diffusion order. Mean-field BK also neglects gluon-number fluctuations, which the FKPP noise corrections must supply.

reason: P1/diffusion is a moment expansion and Fermi age theory is continuous slowing-down, not Chapman–Enskog reductions.

fix.summary: Reactor physics solves the linear Boltzmann transport equation for neutron angular flux, with scattering, absorption and fission sources. The P₁/diffusion approximation (Fick's law, diffusion length) is a low-order angular-moment truncation, and Fermi age theory is a continuous slowing-down treatment of moderation.

reason: e^{-Q/T_f} at 0.8 MeV is ≈1/5, not 1/6. Y_p≈0.25 also needs neutron decay to ~1/7 before the deuterium bottleneck.
Maxwell average times tunnelling is the shared mechanism, a textbook example rather than an identity; strength 2.
Diffusive broadening is the mechanism, not an identity: single hard scatterings give non-Gaussian tails.
Kramers' 1940 paper treated chemical reactions; applying it to fission came later (Grangé–Weidenmüller 1983). It is a method transfer, not historical migration from fission.

fix.summary: Kramers' 1940 theory of thermally activated escape over a barrier, formulated for chemical reactions, was applied to fission by treating the fissioning nucleus as a Brownian particle in a viscous medium. Nuclear dissipation enters as the Kramers factor that reduces the Bohr–Wheeler rate and enhances pre-scission neutron emission.

reason: Poisson statistics and exponential waiting times for decay are textbook and broad; Bateman equations are mean-value ODEs, not a master equation.
Finite-N nuclei only approximate phase transitions with a rounded crossover; this is an analogy needing a breaks, not an identity.

fix.breaks: Nuclei have a finite boson or nucleon number, so there are no true singularities, only rounded crossovers. X(5) and E(5) are idealized critical-point symmetries.

reason: The fourth cumulant scales as ξ⁷, but κσ²=C4/C2 scales as ξ⁵, since C2∝ξ². The (T, μ_B)→(t,h) map is non-universal.

fix.summary: A QCD critical endpoint, if it exists, lies in the 3D Ising (Z₂) universality class. (T, μ_B) map onto Ising (t, h) through a non-universal, generally non-orthogonal transformation. Net-proton cumulants scale as C₄∝ξ⁷ and κσ²∝ξ⁵, so beam-energy scans hunt for non-monotonic kurtosis.

reason: Efimov states are established in cold atoms; nuclear halos are only candidates, so 'seen in light nuclei' overclaims.

fix.summary: Renormalizing the three-boson problem with contact interactions needs a three-body force whose coupling runs periodically in ln Λ: an RG limit cycle rather than a fixed point. This gives discrete scale invariance and the Efimov ratio 22.7, observed in cold atoms and sought in halo nuclei.

fix.breaks: The claimed enhancement factor K depends on nuclear-structure calculations and is still being tested.

reason: Atomic spectroscopy measures a nuclear property: a shared object. The map is dimensionally wrong; it must be m_r³c⁴⟨r²⟩/(ħc)².
Same selection rules and algebra from the same physical cause (multipole radiation), not a named technique that moved across.
The Cs anapole extraction (Wood 1997) is in tension with other nuclear-PNC constraints, so not established.

fix.summary: The nuclear-spin-dependent part of Cs parity violation was interpreted as a nuclear anapole moment, a probe of the parity-violating nucleon–nucleon (weak meson-exchange) interaction.
fix.breaks: The extracted weak pion–nucleon coupling is in tension with other nuclear parity-violation constraints, and the result depends on nuclear-structure modelling.

reason: Wigner introduced random matrices; Dyson developed their classification. Fix attribution.

fix.summary: Wigner introduced random matrices to model neutron-resonance spacings in heavy nuclei, and Dyson classified the ensembles. The nuclear data ensemble later supported the Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit link between classical chaos and Wigner–Dyson statistics.

reason: The link is a shared open question, not a demonstrated common mechanism; ETH has not been tested in the QGP.

fix.breaks: ETH is not established for the expanding QCD system. Hydrodynamization occurs before full thermalization, and the system is open and finite.

reason: Absorb the Kharzeev–Levin attribution from the duplicate C1445. It is a proposal, not settled, and the proton is a pure state.

fix.summary: Kharzeev and Levin proposed that the entanglement entropy between probed and unprobed regions of a proton at small x is S=ln(xG(x)), and compared it with hadron multiplicities in DIS.
fix.breaks: This is model-dependent (saturation, maximal-entanglement assumption). The whole proton is a pure state, and the identification with measured multiplicity entropy is debated.

reason: Same operator form but different physics, so an analogy. The '~20x' claim is wrong: nuclear spin–orbit is order-one relative to shell spacing, versus ~α² for atoms.

fix.breaks: The nuclear spin–orbit term comes from the strong interaction and is comparable to the shell spacing, while atomic fine structure is suppressed by ~α². The level ordering is inverted (j=l+1/2 lies lower in nuclei).

reason: The e^{-2πη} form is the η≫1 limit of the exact Sommerfeld factor 2πη/(e^{2πη}−1), so not an identity. The fusion note is the better b.
TES resolution is set by thermal fluctuations, not the Fano factor, so the map is misleading.
Simulation-based predictions with EOS/neutrino systematics are current research, not textbook-established.
N=4 SYM shock collisions are a model, not an exact dual of QCD heavy-ion collisions, so analogy rather than duality.
Spin-1/2 3He and 129Xe have no quadrupole moment, so they are not Hughes–Drever quadrupole tests. Correct the nuclei.

fix.summary: Hughes–Drever experiments look for sidereal variation of the quadrupole-split NMR or Zeeman spectrum of nuclei with J>1/2 (7Li, 21Ne, 133Cs, 201Hg). Shell-model wavefunctions convert the null results into limits on proton and neutron SME coefficients near 1e-30 GeV.

record.name: Coupled-cluster theory: from nuclei to molecules
record.summary: Coupled-cluster theory was introduced by Coester and Kümmel for nuclear matter (1958–60) and adopted by quantum chemistry (Čížek, Paldus). It now returns to nuclear structure as a polynomially scaling ab initio method reaching 208Pb.
